scope: user-perspective validation of F65 parameter-expansion/substitution-masking fixes (60580c0..d8107d4); adversarial bypass-hunting is out of scope (handled in parallel by security-auditor)

blocking_issues.title: Variable-assign-then-invoke verb obfuscation (V=rm; ${V} <control-plane-file>) is not caught — returns allow, not ask
blocking_issues.description: The verb-position parameter-expansion hardening added by this change (commits 60580c0..d8107d4) only arms a token when __strip_dollar_brace() strips a pure ${VAR} block to EMPTY (undefined/blank assumption) or when an operator-form ${VAR:-...} leaves an unresolved '${' residual. It does not account for the very common, very realistic obfuscation idiom of assigning the verb to a variable earlier in the same command and then referencing it — e.g. `V=rm; ${V} hooks/hooks.json`, `V=rm; ${V} .claude/settings.json`, `DELCMD=rm; $DELCMD hooks/hooks.json`, `A=rm; B=${A}; ${B} hooks/hooks.json`. In every one of these, the firewall returns permissionDecision=allow, and I confirmed by actually running the equivalent in real bash (V=rm; ${V} victim.json) that the file IS deleted. This directly undermines the stated purpose of F65 and of this specific round of commits (catching verb names obscured via parameter expansion/command substitution) for what is arguably the single most natural way a developer (or an obfuscated/injected command) would hide a delete verb behind a variable.
blocking_issues.how_verified: Ran the hook directly via the harness protocol (jq | hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh) for 4 variants, all returned allow. Independently reproduced the real deletion in bash outside the hook to confirm the underlying command is genuinely destructive, not a false alarm.
blocking_issues.note: This is a functional/correctness finding surfaced while doing task item 3 (reading actual ask messages for parameter-expansion-obscured deletes) — these cases never reach the ask message at all, they short-circuit to allow. Flagging because it falls squarely inside the change under review, not as adversarial bypass-hunting; security-auditor may find the same thing independently.

friction_corpus.description: Independently authored corpus of ~30 realistic everyday developer commands using ${VAR}, $(cmd), and backticks in normal (non-adversarial) ways — variable defaults, command substitution for dates/hashes/paths, env var expansion, build/git/k8s operations. None should trigger ask.
friction_corpus.result: 30/30 returned allow — no friction regression detected from the new parameter-expansion/substitution masking logic

commands.command: git commit -m "fix: update parser ($(git rev-parse --short HEAD))"

findings: hooks/hooks.json still registers pre-bash-firewall.sh under PreToolUse with matcher "Bash", timeout 5, invoked as: bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh" — unchanged, correctly wired.

Output shape matches the hook protocol and is consistent with sibling hooks: {hookSpecificOutput: {hookEventName: "PreToolUse", permissionDecision: <allow|ask>, permissionDecisionReason: <string>}} for both allow and ask paths (verified against hooks/pre-tool-firewall.sh, which uses the identical shape for its allow case).

deny path (Layer 1/2 BLOCKED and INDIRECT_PATTERNS) uses exit code 2 with stderr messages (BLOCKED: ... / Pattern: ... / Command: ...) rather than a JSON permissionDecision — this is pre-existing behavior, unchanged by this diff, and consistent with how Claude Code's PreToolUse hook protocol treats a nonzero exit as a hard block.

example.judgment: This generic template (used by most ASK_PATTERNS arms, not the new F65 control-plane-delete arm) dumps the raw grep regex into permissionDecisionReason. That is not legible to an ordinary user and predates this change — not introduced or worsened by 60580c0..d8107d4, so not counted as a blocking regression here, but flagged since it directly bears on 'is the ask message clear enough' for anyone hitting this code path via a control-plane-adjacent editor command.

regression_check_adjacent_features.assessment: These three dependents rely on the exemption/detection wiring (arm_is_exemptable, DETECTED_LOCATIONS, output JSON shape, exit codes) which this diff did not restructure — it only changed how verb tokens are normalized/masked before comparison against ARM_DELETE_VERBS_UNCONDITIONAL. Output shape and exit codes are unchanged (confirmed via direct hook invocation for both allow and ask cases). No structural risk identified for these dependents from this change; not exhaustively re-run.
